location.scope: Bali-wide; verify local and site-specific rules

content.definition: Visitors should keep public spaces and natural environments clean, dispose of waste appropriately, and follow applicable restrictions on single-use plastics.
content.cultural_context: The 2025 Bali Governor Circular prohibits littering or polluting lakes, springs, rivers, seas, and public areas. It also lists plastic bags, Styrofoam, plastic straws, and plastic beverage containers among prohibited single-use plastics for foreign tourists.
content.significance: The guidance applies beyond beaches and attractions to public areas and waterways.
common_situations: Eating or drinking at beaches and public spaces
Visiting rivers, lakes, springs, or coastal areas

do: Use designated waste bins or take waste with you when bins are unavailable
Keep waste away from waterways and beaches
dont: Drop litter in streets, beaches, rivers, lakes, springs, or the sea
Use the specific single-use plastic items prohibited by applicable Bali rules

common_misconceptions: The circular addresses both littering and specified single-use plastic products.
regional_variations: Implementation and waste facilities may differ by location; check local signage and current rules.
content.additional_notes: Do not broaden the exact list of prohibited products without checking the current regulation.

sources.title: Bali Governor Circular Letter No. 07 of 2025 on Foreign Tourist Conduct
Panduan Wajib Wisatawan Asing di Bali: Do's & Don'ts

verification.verification_notes: Prohibitions are directly stated in the Governor Circular and reinforced by Badung tourism guidance.

sensitivity.handling_notes: Use neutral, precise wording; distinguish formal rules from courtesy recommendations.
